nigerianFoods.name: Jollof Rice
nigerianFoods.description: A West African one-pot rice dish cooked in a seasoned tomato and pepper base.
instructions: Blend tomatoes, bell pepper, and part of the onion into a smooth mixture.
Cook sliced onion in oil, add the tomato mixture, and simmer until reduced.
Season the sauce, stir in rice and stock, cover, and cook over low heat until the rice is tender.

nigerianFoods.name: Nigerian Fried Rice
nigerianFoods.description: Rice stir-fried with vegetables and Nigerian curry-seasoned stock.
nigerianFoods.imageAlt: Nigerian fried rice with chicken, sweet corn, carrot, and green peas
instructions: Rinse the rice and parboil it briefly in seasoned stock, then drain.
Dice the vegetables and stir-fry them with onion and curry powder.
Add the rice in batches and stir-fry until heated through and evenly mixed.
nigerianFoods.imageSourceTitle: Fried rice and chicken garnished with sweet corn, carrot and green peas.jpg

nigerianFoods.name: Ofada Rice
nigerianFoods.description: A traditional, aromatic Nigerian rice commonly served with a spicy pepper sauce.
instructions: Pick over the rice and rinse it thoroughly.
Cook in fresh water until the grains are tender, adding water as needed.
Drain excess water and serve hot, traditionally with ayamase sauce.

nigerianFoods.name: Coconut Rice
nigerianFoods.description: Rice simmered with coconut milk and aromatics for a fragrant, gently rich dish.
nigerianFoods.imageAlt: Nigerian coconut rice served on a plate
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear.
Combine rice, coconut milk, stock, sliced onion, thyme, and salt in a pot.
Cover and cook over low heat until tender, then fluff before serving.

nigerianFoods.name: Egusi Soup
nigerianFoods.description: A hearty Nigerian soup thickened with ground melon seeds and leafy vegetables.
instructions: Mix ground egusi with a little water to form a thick paste.
Heat palm oil, add onion and pepper, then cook the egusi paste in small portions.
Add stock and simmer until the soup thickens; stir in leafy vegetables near the end.

nigerianFoods.name: Efo Riro
nigerianFoods.description: A Yoruba spinach stew prepared with peppers, tomatoes, and palm oil.
instructions: Blend the peppers, tomatoes, and part of the onion.
Cook the blended mixture in palm oil until reduced, then add stock and seasoning.
Fold in the washed greens and simmer until just tender.

nigerianFoods.name: Okra Soup
nigerianFoods.description: A draw-textured soup made with chopped okra, stock, and traditional seasonings.
instructions: Wash and finely chop or grate the okra.
Bring stock to a simmer with onion, pepper, and palm oil.
Add the okra and stir until it thickens; add greens and cook briefly.
nigerianFoods.imageSourceTitle: Okra soup, melon soup and catfish stew.jpg

nigerianFoods.name: Ogbono Soup
nigerianFoods.description: A smooth, draw-textured Nigerian soup thickened with ground wild mango seeds.
instructions: Stir ground ogbono into palm oil to make a smooth mixture.
Add the mixture to simmering stock and stir until the soup thickens.
Season to taste, add greens, and simmer until cooked.
nigerianFoods.imageSourceTitle: Ogbono soup with beef and roasted cow skin.jpg

nigerianFoods.name: Afang Soup
nigerianFoods.description: A rich southeastern Nigerian soup featuring finely chopped afang and waterleaf.
instructions: Wash and finely shred the afang and waterleaf separately.
Simmer stock with palm oil, pepper, onion, and seasoning.
Add waterleaf and cook until softened, then stir in afang and simmer briefly.

nigerianFoods.name: Edikaikong Soup
nigerianFoods.description: A vegetable-rich soup from southeastern Nigeria made with pumpkin and waterleaf.
instructions: Wash and slice the vegetables, keeping the pumpkin leaves separate.
Simmer stock with palm oil, onion, pepper, and seasoning.
Add waterleaf and cook until reduced, then fold in pumpkin leaves and cook until tender.

nigerianFoods.name: Oha Soup
nigerianFoods.description: An Igbo soup with tender oha leaves and a thickening base of cocoyam.
instructions: Boil cocoyam until soft, peel, and pound or blend into a smooth paste.
Simmer stock with palm oil, pepper, and seasoning; stir in the cocoyam paste to thicken.
Add shredded oha leaves near the end and cook briefly.
nigerianFoods.imageSourceTitle: Soup and swallow (Oha soup and swallow).jpg

nigerianFoods.name: Banga Soup
nigerianFoods.description: A Niger Delta palm-fruit soup seasoned with fragrant local spices.
instructions: Simmer palm fruit extract until the oil rises to the surface.
Add stock, onion, pepper, and banga spices; cook until the soup thickens.
Add scent leaves shortly before serving.

nigerianFoods.name: Bitterleaf Soup
nigerianFoods.description: A traditional Igbo soup made with washed bitterleaf and a thickening ingredient.
instructions: Boil cocoyam until soft, peel, and pound or blend until smooth.
Simmer stock with palm oil, crayfish, pepper, and seasoning.
Stir in cocoyam paste to thicken, add washed bitterleaf, and simmer until tender.
nigerianFoods.imageSourceTitle: Soup and swallow (Bitterleaf soup and swallow) Nigerian dish.jpg

nigerianFoods.name: Pounded Yam
nigerianFoods.description: A smooth, stretchy swallow traditionally made by pounding cooked yam.
instructions: Peel and cut yam into even chunks, then rinse.
Boil in water until completely tender and drain.
Pound while hot in a mortar, adding small amounts of hot water as needed, until smooth and stretchy.

nigerianFoods.name: Amala
nigerianFoods.description: A soft Yoruba swallow made by stirring yam or cassava flour into hot water.
nigerianFoods.imageAlt: Photograph of amala served with soup
instructions: Bring water to a boil in a pot.
Gradually add yam flour while stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Stir and fold until smooth and firm, then cover briefly before serving.
nigerianFoods.imageSourceTitle: Yam flour swallow and soup (Nigerian cuisine)( Amala).jpg

nigerianFoods.name: Eba
nigerianFoods.description: A firm or soft Nigerian swallow made by mixing garri with hot water.
instructions: Place garri in a heat-safe bowl.
Pour boiling water over the garri gradually while stirring with a wooden spoon.
Knead until smooth and adjust with a little more garri or water to reach the desired firmness.
nigerianFoods.imageSourceTitle: A picture of Eba and Roselle soup.jpg

nigerianFoods.name: Fufu
nigerianFoods.description: A soft, stretchy swallow made from fermented cassava dough or cassava flour.
instructions: If using cassava dough, dissolve it in water and strain to remove lumps.
Cook over medium heat, stirring and folding continuously as it thickens.
Continue until smooth and stretchy; shape and serve warm.

nigerianFoods.name: Tuwo Shinkafa
nigerianFoods.description: A soft northern Nigerian rice swallow prepared by cooking and mashing rice.
nigerianFoods.imageAlt: Tuwo shinkafa served with vegetable soup
instructions: Rinse the rice and add it to a pot with water.
Cook until very soft, adding hot water if needed.
Mash and stir the rice against the side of the pot until it forms a smooth dough.

nigerianFoods.name: Moi Moi
nigerianFoods.description: A steamed savoury bean pudding seasoned with peppers and onion.
instructions: Soak the beans and remove their skins by rubbing and rinsing.
Blend the peeled beans with pepper, onion, and water until smooth; mix in oil and salt.
Pour into heat-safe containers and steam until firm and cooked through.

nigerianFoods.name: Akara
nigerianFoods.description: Crisp Nigerian bean fritters made from peeled black-eyed peas.
nigerianFoods.imageAlt: Photograph of Nigerian akara bean cakes
instructions: Soak the beans and remove their skins, rinsing until clean.
Blend with a small amount of water, onion, pepper, and salt into a thick batter; beat until aerated.
Spoon portions into hot oil and fry, turning, until golden and cooked through.

nigerianFoods.name: Puff Puff
nigerianFoods.description: Soft, lightly sweet Nigerian dough balls fried until golden.
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, and salt; add warm water to make a thick batter.
Cover and leave in a warm place until risen and airy.
Drop small portions into moderately hot oil and fry, turning, until evenly golden.

nigerianFoods.name: Chin Chin
nigerianFoods.description: Crunchy Nigerian bite-sized fried or baked pastry pieces, often served as a snack.
instructions: Combine flour, sugar, and nutmeg, then rub in butter.
Mix in egg and milk to form a firm dough; roll out and cut into small pieces.
Fry in batches until golden, or bake until crisp, then cool before serving.

nigerianFoods.name: Nigerian Meat Pie
nigerianFoods.description: A savoury baked pastry filled with seasoned minced meat and vegetables.
nigerianFoods.imageAlt: Photograph of a meat pie from Northern Nigeria
instructions: Cook minced beef with onion, diced potato, carrot, and seasoning until the filling is tender; cool it.
Rub butter into flour, add cold water, and bring together into pastry dough; chill briefly.
Fill pastry rounds, seal and glaze with beaten egg, then bake until golden.

nigerianFoods.name: Suya
nigerianFoods.description: Nigerian-style skewered meat coated in a spicy peanut and chilli seasoning.
instructions: Combine ground peanuts with ginger, paprika, cayenne, and salt.
Thread thin beef slices onto skewers and coat with the spice mixture.
Grill or broil, turning regularly, until browned and cooked through; serve with sliced onion.

nigerianFoods.name: Pepper Soup
nigerianFoods.description: A light, aromatic Nigerian broth seasoned with chilli and pepper-soup spices.
nigerianFoods.imageAlt: Goat meat pepper soup served with bread
instructions: Place the cleaned fish or meat in a pot with onion, pepper, and water.
Add pepper-soup spice and simmer until the protein is cooked and the broth is fragrant.
Stir in scent leaves and salt, then simmer briefly before serving.
nigerianFoods.imageSourceTitle: Goat meat pepper soup served with bread.jpg

nigerianFoods.name: Yam Porridge
nigerianFoods.description: A one-pot Nigerian dish of yam cubes simmered with pepper, onion, and palm oil.
nigerianFoods.imageAlt: Nigerian yam pottage, also called asaro
instructions: Peel and cut yam into bite-sized cubes, then rinse.
Simmer yam with stock, onion, pepper, and palm oil until nearly tender.
Mash a few pieces into the liquid to thicken, add greens, and cook until tender.

nigerianFoods.name: Beans Porridge
nigerianFoods.description: A filling Nigerian bean dish cooked slowly with onion, pepper, and palm oil.
nigerianFoods.imageAlt: Nigerian beans porridge served with fried plantains
instructions: Rinse the beans and place them in a pot with water and sliced onion.
Cook until the beans are tender, adding hot water as needed.
Stir in palm oil, pepper, and salt; simmer until the liquid thickens.

nigerianFoods.name: Beans and Plantain
nigerianFoods.description: A familiar Nigerian combination of soft beans and ripe plantain, served together.
instructions: Cook rinsed beans with onion and water until soft.
Season the beans with palm oil, pepper, and salt and simmer until creamy.
Peel and boil or fry the plantain separately, then serve with the beans.

nigerianFoods.name: Abacha
nigerianFoods.description: An Igbo African salad made with shredded cassava, palm oil, and fresh garnishes.
nigerianFoods.imageAlt: Abacha, also known as African salad
instructions: Soak abacha in warm water until soft, then drain thoroughly.
Mix palm oil with the chosen seasoning and stir into the abacha.
Fold in ugba, sliced onion, garden egg, and fresh leaves; serve promptly.

nigerianFoods.name: Nkwobi
nigerianFoods.description: A traditional Igbo dish of tender cow foot coated in a spicy palm-oil sauce.
nigerianFoods.imageAlt: Nkwobi garnished with utazi leaves and onions
instructions: Clean and cook cow foot with onion and salt until very tender.
Stir a small amount of potash solution into palm oil until the mixture thickens and changes colour.
Mix in pepper and crayfish, coat the cooked cow foot, and garnish with utazi and onion.

nigerianFoods.name: Isi Ewu
nigerianFoods.description: A celebratory Igbo dish of goat head pieces in a spiced palm-oil sauce.
instructions: Clean and cut the goat head into pieces; cook with onion and salt until tender.
Mix palm oil with a little potash solution until thickened, then add pepper and crayfish.
Coat the cooked pieces with the sauce and garnish with sliced utazi and onion.

nigerianFoods.name: Asaro (Yam Pottage)
nigerianFoods.description: A Yoruba-style yam pottage in which yam cooks down into a soft, savoury stew.
nigerianFoods.imageAlt: Asaro yam porridge served with fried beef
instructions: Peel and cube yam, then rinse.
Cook onion, tomatoes, and pepper in palm oil; add stock and yam.
Cover and simmer until yam is tender, mashing some pieces into the sauce; stir in greens before serving.

nigerianFoods.name: Ukwa (African Breadfruit)
nigerianFoods.description: A traditional Igbo dish of African breadfruit simmered until soft and savoury.
nigerianFoods.imageAlt: Ukwa African breadfruit served ready to eat
instructions: Sort and rinse the breadfruit thoroughly.
Cook in plenty of water until the grains are tender, adding water as needed.
Season with onion, pepper, palm oil, and salt; simmer until the liquid is absorbed.

nigerianFoods.name: Gbegiri
nigerianFoods.description: A Yoruba bean soup made from peeled beans and traditionally paired with ewedu and stew.
nigerianFoods.imageAlt: Gbegiri with amala and ewedu soup
instructions: Soak beans and remove the skins, then rinse.
Boil the beans until very soft and mash or blend until smooth.
Return to low heat, stir in palm oil and pepper, and season to taste.
nigerianFoods.imageSourceTitle: Amala and Gbegiri with Ewedu soup.jpg

nigerianFoods.name: Ewa Agoyin
nigerianFoods.description: Very soft-cooked beans served with a deeply browned, peppery onion sauce.
instructions: Cook rinsed beans in water until very soft, then lightly mash.
Soak dried peppers and blend or grind them coarsely.
Fry sliced onion in palm oil until deeply browned, add pepper, and cook into a thick sauce; serve over the beans.

nigerianFoods.name: Dodo (Fried Plantain)
nigerianFoods.description: Ripe plantain slices fried until caramelized and golden, commonly served as a side or snack.
instructions: Peel the plantain and slice diagonally or into rounds.
Heat a shallow layer of oil in a pan.
Fry the slices in batches, turning once, until golden and caramelized; drain and serve.
